static_evidence_items.content: Chief complaint: asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
Medical history: chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
Medical history: refractory anemia with excess blasts
Physical examination finding: 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
Skin Biopsy: diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells admixed with rare eosinophils
Skin Biopsy: uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
BRAF-V600E variant status identified through immunohistochemical studies and confirmed by polymerase chain reaction analysis
Bone Marrow Biopsy: hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts
Molecular Analysis: identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
Figure 1A: Red papule under the right lower eyelid
Figure 1B: Atypical diffuse dermal monocytoid-appearing infiltrate admixed with eosinophils (hematoxylin-eosin; original magnification ×40)
Figure 1C: Immunohistochemical studies reveal strong positivity for langerin (original magnification ×20)
